# Light shifts {.unnumbered #light-shifts-theory}

## Complex spectral response {#complex-spectral-response}

The same complex Voigt response is used for absorption and AC Stark shifts. Its real part supplies the absorptive optical-pumping profile; its imaginary part supplies the dispersive light shift. This keeps the two responses consistent when detuning is comparable to the Doppler width.

## Scalar, vector, and tensor components {#light-shift-components}

Within one hyperfine manifold, the diagonal shift is decomposed as

$$
\nu(F,m)=\nu_{\mathrm{scalar}}
+c_{\mathrm{vector}}m
+c_{\mathrm{tensor}}\left[3m^2-F(F+1)\right].
$$

The scalar contribution shifts the manifold without distinguishing (m). The vector contribution acts like a fictitious magnetic field. The tensor contribution produces an (m^2)-dependent splitting.

## Use in the RF solver {#light-shifts-in-rf-response}

The state frequency used by the secular RF solver is

$$
\nu_a=\nu_{B,a}+\nu_{\mathrm{LS},a}.
$$

Adjacent transition frequencies are differences of these state frequencies. Consequently, pump detuning and intensity can move individual RF resonances even when the pump is used only as a weak optical detector.
